newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-HENTGEN OUTDUELS PETTITTE AS BLUE JAYS NIP YANKS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-HENTGEN OUTDUELS PETTITTE AS BLUE JAYS NIP YANKS.

text.p: Pat Hentgen edged Andy Pettitte last year to win the American League Cy Young Award and the hard-throwing right-hander outdueled the talented lefty again Tuesday as the Toronto Blue Jays beat the Yankees 2-0.
Hentgen, backed by superb defence, tossed a five-hitter for his second shutout of the season, while a pair of costly errors hurt the Yankees in a tense pitcher's duel.
"If you can't get up for pitching at Yankee Stadium, something's wrong with you," said Hentgen (4-1). "The defence played awesome, and you need those things, and tonight I got them."

In the sixth, first baseman Tino Martinez misplayed Otis Nixon's bunt and Orlando Merced hit a perfect double-play grounder to second baseman Mariano Duncan, but the ball hit off his knee and flew into the air. Merced was safe and Nixon cruised into third.
Joe Carter then drove in the game's first run with a single to left. In the eighth, Carlos Garcia doubled and scored on Merced's single off hard-luck loser Pettitte (6-2).
"It was a great game, one of the better ones this year," Toronto manager Cito Gaston said. "Hentgen showed why he won the Cy Young, and Pettitte showed why he was considered for the award."
"They played a better defensive game," said Yankee manager Joe Torre. "Andy matched Pat pitch for pitch. They made the plays and we didn't."
In Anaheim, Tim Salmon snapped an 0-for-15 slump with a homer and three-run double that capped an eighth-inning rally as the Angels outslugged the Seattle Mariners 11-9.
Salmon ended his drought in the fourth with his sixth homer. But it was his bases-loaded double in the bottom of the eighth that turned a one-run deficit into an 11-9 advantage.
Garret Anderson went 2-for-5, extending his hitting streak to 16 games for the Angels, who have won eight of nine.

Rich DeLucia (4-1) got the win, despite allowing three runs in two innings in relief of starter Jason Dickson. Troy Percival, back from injury, got the side in order in the ninth for his first save of the season.
Seattle star Ken Griffey Jr. hit his major-league leading 20th homer and pushed his league-leading RBI total to 55.
In Chicago, Jaime Navarro allowed one run in eight innings to beat Boston for the 10th straight time and Harold Baines drove in three as the White Sox walloped the Red Sox 10-1.
Navarro (4-2) allowed six hits and walked one with five strikeouts in improving to 11-3 lifetime against Boston.
Chicago won their fifth straight.

Frank Thomas fell just shy of the major-league record for consecutive times reaching base, getting stopped at 15 straight when he flew out to centre field in the fifth inning. Ted Williams set the record of 16 in 1957.
"This would have been a nice record for Frank to go along with everything else that he'll accomplished in his career," Chicago manager Terry Bevington said.
"They'll say that Frank Thomas was the best hitter of his time and that's fitting because they say that Ted Williams was the best hitter of his time."
At Texas, Bobby Witt set a team record with his seventh straight win to start the season as the Rangers defeated the reeling Oakland Athletics 8-3.
Warren Newson went 4-for-5 with two doubles and a triple, while Bill Ripken, Rusty Greer and Lee Stevens homered for the winners.
Former Ranger Jose Canseco and Geronimo Berroa hit solo homers for the Athletics, who have lost four straight and 11 of their last 13 games.
Ariel Prieto (3-3) took the loss.
In Cleveland, Manny Ramirez hit a two-run homer in the bottom of the eighth to lead the Cleveland Indians to a 4-3 victory over the Kansas City Royals.

The Indians trailed 3-0 after six innings but scored a pair of runs in the seventh to cut the deficit to 3-2. In the eighth, David Justice led off with a single before Ramirez homered off reliever Jamie Walker (2-2).
Paul Shuey (1-1) picked up the win in relief. Cleveland's Julio Franco extend his hitting streak to a major-league best 18 games with a first-inning double.

In Baltimore, Scott Kamieniecki pitched 7 2/3 strong innings and Rafael Palmeiro highlighted a four-run fourth with a two-run single to lead the Baltimore Orioles to their fourth straight win, 4-3 over the Detroit Tigers.
Kamieniecki (3-2) allowed three runs and four hits. Randy Myers pitched a scoreless ninth for his 14th save, tying him with New York's Mariano Rivera for the American League lead.
Omar Olivares (2-3) suffered the loss as Baltimore improved to a league best 16-7 at home.
In Milwaukee, Scott Stahoviak smacked a two-run homer to boost the Minnesota Twins to some rare success with a 4-3 win over the slumping Brewers.
Mike Trombley (1-0) tossed 2 2/3 innings of scoreless relief as the Twins won consecutive games for the first time in a month in handing Milwaukee its seventh straight loss.
